# skald

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/JamesHWade/skald/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JamesHWade/skald/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![pkgdown](https://github.com/JamesHWade/skald/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JamesHWade/skald/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

skald provides tidy R interfaces to ColBERT-style late-interaction
retrieval, reranking, scoring, and indexing. The first backend wraps
[PyLate](https://lightonai.github.io/pylate/) through
[reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/), while keeping model,
index, and embedding objects opaque in R.

The package boundary is intentionally narrow:

- ragnar ingests, chunks, stores, and performs first-stage retrieval.
- skald encodes, reranks, scores, indexes, and retrieves with late interaction.
- dsprrr can compose retrievers into declarative RAG pipelines.

## Installation

You can install the development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JamesHWade/skald")
```

Like ragnar, skald uses reticulate's managed Python environment support. When
the package loads, it sets `RETICULATE_PYTHON = "managed"` and records the
PyLate requirement with `reticulate::py_require()`. Run setup to force an
environment check before loading a model:

```r
library(skald)

skald_setup()
skald_sitrep()
```

## Rerank ragnar results

The most common workflow is to use ragnar for candidate generation and skald
for late-interaction reranking.

```r
library(ragnar)
library(skald)

model <- skald_model("lightonai/GTE-ModernColBERT-v1", device = "cpu")

query <- "How can I subset a dataframe with a logical vector?"

hits <- ragnar_retrieve(store, query, top_k = 50)

hits |>
  skald_rerank(
    model,
    query = query,
    text = text,
    id = c(origin, doc_id, chunk_id),
    top_k = 5
  )
```

`skald_rerank()` preserves the original columns, appends `late_score` and
`late_rank`, orders by late-interaction score, and keeps first-stage order as
the tie breaker.

## Build a skald store

`SkaldStore` keeps chunk metadata in DuckDB and the late-interaction index in
PyLate's PLAID format.

```r
chunks <- "https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html" |>
  ragnar::read_as_markdown() |>
  ragnar::markdown_chunk()

store <- skald_store_create(
  "r4ds.skald",
  model = model,
  name = "r4ds",
  title = "R for Data Science"
)

skald_store_insert(store, chunks)
skald_store_build_index(store)

skald_retrieve(store, "How do I filter rows?", top_k = 5)
```

Chunk identifiers are stable and string-valued. For ragnar markdown chunks,
they are derived from the source origin and character positions rather than
from ragnar's auto-incrementing store IDs.

## Standalone PyLate index

skald can also manage a low-level PLAID index without ragnar.

```r
docs <- tibble::tibble(
  doc_id = c("1", "2", "3"),
  text = c(
    "ColBERT keeps token-level embeddings for fine-grained retrieval.",
    "PLAID compresses token vectors for scalable search.",
    "PyLate trains and retrieves with late-interaction models."
  )
)

index <- skald_index_create("demo-index", overwrite = TRUE)

index <- skald_index_add(
  index,
  model,
  docs,
  id = doc_id,
  text = text
)

skald_index_retrieve(
  index,
  model,
  query = "What library supports ColBERT retrieval?",
  top_k = 3
)
```

## Score semantics

Late-interaction scores are query-relative MaxSim scores. Higher scores are
better, but they are not probabilities, are not bounded to `[0, 1]`, and should
not be compared against universal thresholds.

## Design notes

skald follows tidyverse package conventions where they help retrieval workflows:
data-frame APIs use tidy evaluation, return tibbles, preserve columns, and keep
Python objects out of user-visible columns unless explicitly requested.
